original_question: Find an analogue, in the borderline case omega_H-infinity(A) = pi/2, of the characterizations known below the critical angle. On Hilbert spaces, if -A generates a contractive analytic C_0-semigroup then A has a bounded H-infinity calculus with omega_H-infinity(A) = omega(A) < pi/2, and conversely operators with bounded H-infinity calculus of angle less than pi/2 are similar to generators of contractive analytic semigroups. On L^p-spaces, if -A generates a contractive positive analytic C_0-semigroup then A has a bounded H-infinity calculus with angle less than pi/2, and conversely such operators admit the structural model described in Theorem 2.11. What is the correct corresponding characterization when the H-infinity angle is exactly pi/2?
target_in_paper: The L^p critical-angle open problem posed in Section 2 immediately after the discussion culminating in Theorem 2.11: whether, for 1<p<infinity, the generator -A of a contractive C_0-semigroup on an L^p-space must satisfy that A has a bounded H^infty-calculus with omega_{H^infty}(A) <= pi/2.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's surrounding theme: the known subcritical (< pi/2) results linking bounded H^infty-calculus to contractive/positive analytic semigroups on Hilbert and L^p spaces, and it correctly focuses attention on the borderline angle pi/2. It also correctly treats Theorem 2.11 as part of the relevant nearby context.
missing_details: The paper's nearest official formulation at the critical angle is not a two-sided characterization; it is a one-way open problem.
At the borderline pi/2, the paper asks about generators of contractive C_0-semigroups, not necessarily analytic semigroups.
The ambient space in the nearest formulation is an L^p-space with 1<p<infinity.
The question should be stated for some L^p(omega)-space, not abstractly for all Banach spaces or simultaneously for Hilbert and L^p spaces.
The conclusion sought is exactly: A has a bounded H^infty-calculus with omega_{H^infty}(A) <= pi/2.
Positivity is part of the known subcritical sufficient condition, but it is not part of the critical-angle open problem as formulated nearest to your draft.
The structural converse below pi/2 from Theorem 2.11 is background and motivation, not part of the critical-angle question itself.
Your draft asks for a 'corresponding characterization' at angle exactly pi/2, but the paper does not formulate the borderline issue that broadly.
To be stand-alone, the question should specify that -A is the generator and A is the operator whose H^infty-angle is being asked about.
The paper immediately broadens the same question to uniformly convex Banach spaces, but that broader variant is secondary, not the nearest formulation.
refined_question: Let 1<p<infinity, let X=L^p(Omega), and let -A be the generator of a contractive C_0-semigroup on X. Must A admit a bounded H^infty-calculus with critical angle omega_{H^infty}(A) <= pi/2?
justification: The paper's official borderline question is narrower than your draft. In the nearby Section 2 discussion, the author first records the known subcritical results, including the L^p structural theorem in Theorem 2.11 for the case omega_{H^infty}(A)<pi/2. The natural critical-angle question then asked in the paper is not a full analogue or characterization at omega_{H^infty}(A)=pi/2, but specifically whether every generator of a contractive C_0-semigroup on an L^p-space already has bounded H^infty-calculus with angle at most pi/2. That is the closest paper-faithful stand-alone question. Your draft is therefore directionally right but too broad: it imports the subcritical converse/structure theory into the borderline regime, whereas the paper only singles out the forward implication as the open problem, and then notes an even broader uniformly convex variant.
